result.description:
All Industries Group is an innovative, multi-disciplined design, engineering and fabrication specialist. Focusing on product supply and turnkey solutions for local, national and international clients.

All Industries Group is a family owned and run manufacturing business on the central coast of Yeppoon, Qld, with its team built with the most experienced, skillful, and committed employees, is the largest manufacturing company in Livingstone Shire.

All Industries strives to set the standard of what quality looks like in the advanced manufacturing space, through our systems and culture. We are dedicated to ensuring the business is run with its employees in mind. This is accomplished through our core values which are at the centre of everything we do. These include Quality, Teamwork, Family, Integrity, and Education.

We are seeking experienced DRAFTSPERSON/ PLANNER to join our busy workshop on a full time and permanent basis.

The role includes but is not limited to:
To carry out design and development of produce including design verification and validation.
Ensuring all work is carried out in accordance with All Industries Group policies and procedures
Calculate dimensions, weight limitations and requirements in materials
Describe production methods step-by-step (including equipment and software types to be used)
Create detailed designs with Inventor and AutoCAD software
Design diagrams, maps and layouts to illustrate workflow
Identify potential operational issues and redesign products to improve functionality
Ensure final designs comply with AS/NZ & ISO standards, regulations and quality standards
Create manuals that describe existing products’ operation, features and maintenance, eg. Dossiers, close our reports etc
Provide quotations and updates to customers when required
Creating and control of production orders following AIG’s procedures using ERP system (ITMS)
Daily update of Work In Progress (WIP), job schedule and communicate information with the rest of the production team (5 day production schedule minimum)
Liaise with the production supervisor to ensure jobs are meeting deadlines, within budget hours and are meeting Quality Assessment (QA)
Encourage and maintain acceptable QA and Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
Maintain accuracy and up to date data in AIG’s Electronic Resource Planner (ERP) System (ITMS) and server drives
Include information on project planning/management, estimation & profitability
Raise NCR’s, recommend corrective action, and offer suggestions for improvement
Participate in weekly production meetings and engineering meetings
Carry out design and development of products, including verification and validation of designs
To ensure all records, including drawing numbers etc are up to date
Develop defined scope of works for tenders and attend to site/jobs when required
To ensure all communication is engaged with internal, external and third-party contractors
To report to the Management System Manager (MSM)
Undertake training for professional development and coaching and be involved in AIG’s competitive business systems (Lean/Six Sigma)

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
At least with more than 4-years of experience in the same trade
Ability to work well both independently and in a team environment
Strong communication skills
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

result.description:
Target Business Services

Location: 91-109 Main Neerim Road, Neerim South, Victoria 3831
Salary: $80,000 plus 12% superannuation
Position: Full time, Permanent

Our client, AFS Consulting Group Pty. Ltd. trading as Neerim South Hotel, is a well-established hospitality venue located in the heart of Neerim South, Victoria. The hotel offers quality accommodation, a popular bistro, bar facilities, and function spaces, providing a welcoming destination for both local patrons and visitors. The business is committed to delivering high standards of customer service, quality dining, and memorable guest experiences.

The business is seeking to appoint an experienced Hotel Manager to oversee the day-to-day operations of the hotel, ensuring efficient service delivery across accommodation, food and beverage, and front-of-house operations. The primary purpose of this role is to manage operational performance, lead the hospitality team, maintain compliance with industry regulations, and contribute to the hotel's continued commercial success.

This role is integral to maintaining the hotel's reputation for quality hospitality while driving operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, and business growth.

Minimum Requirements:

-	Diploma or equivalent qualification as recognised under the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF). A qualification in Hospitality Management, Business, or a related discipline is highly desirable.
-	Minimum one year of relevant experience in a similar management role within the hospitality industry.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Oversee the daily operations of the hotel, including accommodation, bar, bistro, functions, and customer service activities.
-	Monitor operational performance to ensure high standards of guest service, cleanliness, and presentation are consistently maintained.
-	Recruit, supervise, train, and evaluate staff while fostering a productive and customer-focused workplace culture.
-	Manage guest enquiries, complaints, and service issues promptly to ensure high levels of customer satisfaction.
-	Prepare budgets, monitor financial performance, control operating costs, and provide regular reports to the Director.
-	Ensure compliance with liquor licensing, food safety, workplace health and safety, and all relevant regulatory requirements.
-	Coordinate maintenance programs and liaise with contractors to ensure hotel facilities remain safe and well maintained.
-	Manage purchasing, inventory, and supplier relationships to maintain efficient stock control and cost-effective operations.
-	Develop and implement promotional initiatives, functions, and local marketing activities to increase patronage and revenue.
-	Monitor customer feedback and implement continuous improvements to enhance operational performance and guest experience.

Skills and Experience:

-	Demonstrated leadership and team management skills within a hospitality environment.
-	Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with a strong customer service focus.
-	Sound financial management skills, including budgeting, cost control, and performance reporting.
-	Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities in a fast-paced operational environment.
-	Excellent organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple operational functions.
-	Knowledge of hospitality operations, food and beverage service, accommodation management, and venue promotions.
-	Thorough understanding of relevant hospitality legislation, including liquor licensing, food safety, workplace health and safety, and employment obligations.

To apply, please send your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au
Please note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

About our Organisation 
VENTORA is the name behind iconic Australian brands including A&L Windows & Doors, Breezway louvres, Corinthian Doors, Stegbar Windows & Doors and Trend Windows & Doors.
As an established manufacturer with over 4,500 employees, our vision is to inspire our customers through leading brands, great service, innovative new products and solutions leveraging the full VENTORA portfolio, while significantly enhancing our ease of doing business built on operational excellence.

About the Opportunity
We are currently seeking an experienced Operational Excellence & COPQ (Cost Of Poor Quality) Transformation Specialist to join our committed team.
Reporting directly to our Chief Transformation Officer and indirectly to our Chief Manufacturing Officer, you will be responsible for driving operational excellence across all VENTORA Group manufacturing sites. Your focus will be accelerating the reduction of COPQ, supporting Transformation projects and preparing sites for scalable growth. This role is key in ensuring the readiness of Red List sites and ensuring that manufacturing processes are optimized to support business growth targets, including a 2x increase in in capacity.
Responsibilities include:
•	Drive COPQ Reduction Across Sites: Lead initiatives to identify, address, and reduce COPQ at each manufacturing site, fast-tracking reduction actions.
•	Support Transformation Projects: Provide operational support for the successful execution of Transformation Projects, aiming to modernize manufacturing processes and systems.
•	Red List Site Support: Work directly with Red List sites to build operational foundations and enhance manufacturing readiness for growth, ensuring these sites meet operational standards.
•	Enhance Manufacturing Efficiency: Identify and implement process improvements that reduce downtime, improve throughput, and optimize resource utilization across sites.
•	Leadership Support: Assist site leaders in improving operational performance, driving COPQ reduction, and supporting data-driven decision-making to foster a culture of continuous improvement. 
•	Operational Systems and Process Standardization: Work closely with local Operational Managers to develop and standardize operational systems, quality control, and inventory management processes across all sites.
•	Cross-functional Collaboration: Collaborate with various departments to ensure alignment and successful execution of operational goals, focusing on operational excellence, cost-saving initiatives, and continuous improvement.

About You
You will bring the following skills and experience:
•	Manufacturing Leadership: Extensive senior operational management experience with a track record of improving plant operations, driving site performance, driving manufacturing excellence and achieving performance targets in a multi-site environment. 
•	COPQ Expertise: Proven track record in reducing COPQ and implementing strategies to improve product quality and profitability across manufacturing sites.
•	Operational Excellence: Deep knowledge of lean manufacturing, process optimization, and cost-saving initiatives to enhance operational performance.
•	Cross-functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively across functions to drive transformation projects and foster a collaborative, high-performance culture.
•	People Development: Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop operational leaders and foster a culture of continuous improvement.
•	Results-Oriented: A focus on achieving measurable results and driving continuous improvement across all operational areas.
•	Time Management: Effective time management and organizational skills to prioritize tasks, manage workloads, and ensure deadlines are met.
•	Innovation: Ability to think outside the box and implement innovative solutions to improve manufacturing processes and drive operational excellence.
•	Adaptability: Ability to manage change and navigate ambiguity in a fast-paced environment.
•	Driver’s License: Hold a current unrestricted driver’s license to perform the requirements of the role.
•	Educational Qualification: A diploma or degree in a relevant discipline (business, engineering, manufacturing) or equivalent experience is preferred.

About the Benefits
•	Permanent, full time role with established industry leader
•	Annual salary: $150,000 - $180,000 (depending on experience) + super.
•	Flexible work arrangements, with 2 days per week WFH
•	Generous discounts on our extensive range of products
•	Ability to schedule leave every year over the Christmas period.
•	Additional paid day’s leave on your birthday
•	Flare benefits program - salary packaging, discounts and premium perks
•	Employee Assistance Program access
•	Career progression opportunities as part of a 4,500-employee organisation

Known for delivering quality outcomes and maintaining long standing client relationships. With the major high rise residential project now entering the finishing stages, they are seeking an experienced Site Supervisor to drive quality, safety, and timely delivery.   Your new role:  As the Site Supervisor overseeing finishing works, you will manage day to day site operations across internal fitout and final presentation stages. You will coordinate trades, monitor progress, uphold safety standards, and ensure workmanship meets project specifications. Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Supervising finishing trades across apartments, common areas, and amenities 
 Managing daily site activities, toolbox talks, and safety compliance 
 Reviewing quality of works and driving defect resolution 
 Coordinating subcontractors and sequencing works to meet program milestones 
 Liaising with the Project Manager, Site Manager, and client representatives 
 Maintaining site documentation, reporting, and progress updates 
 This role is critical to achieving a high quality handover and ensuring the project meets its delivery targets. 
 
   What you'll need to succeed:  
 
 Proven experience as a Site Supervisor on highrise residential or commercial projects 
 Strong finishing works background across fitout, joinery, services, and final presentation 
 Excellent communication and subcontractor management skills 
 Ability to read and interpret drawings, specifications, and programs 
 A proactive approach to safety, quality, and problem solving 
 White Card and relevant trade or construction qualifications 
 
  What you'll get in return:  You'll join a builder with a strong reputation, supportive leadership, and a secure project pipeline. Expect competitive remuneration, long term career progression, and the opportunity to deliver a landmark Western Sydney project. result.description: SKS BUILDERS PTY LTD   About SKS Group Australia   SKS Group Australia is a privately owned Australian company established in 2011. The Group operates as a diversified organisation with core business interests spanning property development, investment holdings, hospitality, and credit finance.  Our vision is to deliver landmark developments in strategic locations, maintaining exceptional standards of quality, innovation, and sustainability. These projects include premium residential, commercial, and hospitality. Since its establishment, SKS Builders has successfully completed numerous multi-million-dollar developments, including the construction of both DoubleTree by Hilton properties in Perth. Coordinate the timely delivery of materials, equipment, and services to support uninterrupted project delivery.  Assist with procurement processes, supplier engagement, and contract administration activities.    On-Site Health, Safety and Compliance    Promote and maintain a safe working environment on site.  Assist with site inductions, toolbox meetings, and safety inspections.  Monitor compliance with workplace health and safety legislation, regulations, and company policies.  Report hazards, incidents, and non-conformances to management and assist in implementing corrective actions.  Ensure all site activities comply with relevant building codes, permits, approvals, and company procedures.    Quality Assurance    Assist in implementing project quality assurance procedures.  Conduct routine inspections of workmanship and materials on site.  Identify defects and coordinate corrective actions with subcontractors and suppliers.  Maintain accurate records of inspections, defects, rectification works, and quality outcomes.  Support the delivery of projects that meet client expectations and regulatory requirements.    Stakeholder Communication    Liaise with subcontractors, consultants, suppliers, clients, and regulatory authorities as directed.  Support effective communication between office and site teams.  Report site productivity and data to stakeholders, ensuring technical progress is communicated clearly to local management and HQ in Malaysia.  Attend project meetings and provide technical reporting and operational support where required.  Assist in resolving site-related issues promptly and professionally.  Foster positive working relationships with all project stakeholders.    Post-Construction Handover and Defect Management Support    Assist with the coordinating post-construction defect rectifications and handover maintenance across completed buildings during the defects liability period.  Conduct building inspections and identify maintenance requirements, defects, or compliance issues.  Coordinate contractors and service providers to undertake maintenance and remedial works.  Monitor maintenance schedules and ensure works are completed within agreed timeframes and budgets.  Maintain accurate records of inspections, maintenance activities, warranties, asset registers, and compliance documentation.    Building Compliance and Regulatory Support    Interpret and apply building plans, specifications, building codes, Australian Standards, and relevant legislation. MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Project Officer (ASO4)





Job no: 942871

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Administration, Business and Management




 

Department for Health and Wellbeing - Strategy and Governance - Governance Advisory Services, Legal & Legislative Policy

Salary: $79,432 to $83,266 - ASO4 - Full Time - Term Contract up to 12 Months

Role Details:

Working as a Project Officer in a small, highly skilled team, you will operate in a diverse and intellectually stimulating environment to provide an effective and efficient claims service, across SA Health, for the classes of insurance managed in-house by Insurance Services team.

The role offers exposure to a broad range of complex insurance, claims management, governance and risk-rated matters, providing opportunities to collaborate with senior stakeholders, analyse data and support strategic decision-making.

The Project Officer will develop and maintain close working relationships with officers across SA Health, the South Australian Government Financing Authority (SAFA), Loss Assessors and health related Non-Government Organisation, to ensure effective delivery of Governance Advisory projects and SA Health's Insurance Services.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

Manage competing priorities with professionalism and agility, delivering high-quality outcomes in a dynamic environment, while maintaining strong record management practices and contributing to a collaborative, high-performing team culture.

Assist with the administration, development and review of SA Health's insurance services functions managed the Insurance Services team.

Conduct an initial assessment of reported incidents, (hospital visitor, data breach) ensuring information is accurate and complete in all respects and advise the client on management of issues associated with incidents.

Conduct an initial assessment of reported claims, Property, Public Liability and Professional Indemnity and make claim determination.

Advise the client whether the incident is an approved claim under the insurance program and manage the claim through to completion.

Compile SA Health's yearly questionnaire response to (SAFA), involving analysing data integrity and follow-up of submitted questionnaire returns by LHNs-SAAS-NGOs and briefing the CE for approval prior to submission to SAFA.

To be successful you will have:

The ability to communicate both orally and in writing with a wide range of individuals and organisations, including consumers, community or professional groups, departmental, Local government, and other State Government officers at varying levels and to exercise discretion in relation to sensitive issues and maintain confidentiality.

The ability to research and gather information relevant to Insurance Services, and project development using analytical and investigative skills, and to draft high-quality briefings, minutes and reports.

Good interpersonal and conflict resolution skills which contribute to the development of effective working relationships with a wide range of people, and which foster trust and cooperation.

Effective skills in time management, including the ability to organise workflow to determine priorities and meet deadlines while working with limited direction.

A strong commitment and demonstrated ability to maintain flexibility, contribute as a team member and value diversity.

Demonstrated ability to organise, implement and coordinate concurrent projects and to successfully manage programs and projects of some complexity.

Ability to interpret and understand policies and instructions.

If this sounds like you, then we encourage you to apply.

Why you'll love it here - benefits that matter:

We know a great career is about more than the work you do. It is also about feeling supported, valued, and able to thrive. At SA Health, you will enjoy:

A collaborative team environment, working alongside people committed to best practice and meaningful impact.

Flexible work options and tailored arrangements to help you balance work and life.

Recognition and growth, celebrating achievements and supporting development opportunities across SA Health.

Health and fitness perks, including discounted Fitness Passport memberships and free flu vaccinations.

Wellbeing support, including confidential Employee Assistance Program services for you and your family.

About Us:

The Department for Health and Wellbeing assists the Minister for Health and Wellbeing to set the policy framework and strategic directions for SA Health. The Department supports the delivery of public health services, formulates health policy, facilitates public and consumer consultation on health issues, and monitors the performance of South Australia's health system by providing timely advice, research and administrative support.

The Legal and Legislative Policy Unit sits within the Governance Advisory Services branch of SA Health's Strategy and Governance Division. The Legal and Legislative Policy Unit facilitates the provision of Legal, Governance, and Insurance advice to the Minister for Health and Wellbeing; the Chief Executive of the Department for Health and Wellbeing; the Executive Director, Governance Advisory Services; and all SA Health Staff.

Department for Health and Wellbeing - Integrated Care Systems - Clinical System Support & Improvement

Salary: $123,048 to $133,957 - AHP4 - Full Time - Term Contract up to 23 Months

Overview:

The Clinical Program Manager will provide advice, leadership, management and clinical knowledge for state-wide strategic projects and reform initiatives related to the Department for Health and Wellbeing (DHW) Hospital in the Home and community based post-acute services, with a focus on health (including mental health), aged care, disability, and priority populations. They will be required to:

Coordinate projects relevant to the implementation of Hospital in the Home and community-based post-acute services with relevant community-based stakeholders.

Provide advice, leadership, management, and knowledge of the Hospital in the Home and community based post-acute service implementation and related initiatives to DHW and SA Government agencies as required.

Significantly contribute to the Hospital Community Integration Team and Integrated Care Systems Directorate.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Job ref: 944806

Criminal History Screening Requirement

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment).

A DHS 'Working With Children Check' (WWCC) is required for this position.

Immunisation Risk for this position is Category C (minimal patient contact).

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Special Condition

Appropriate degree or equivalent qualification which gives eligibility for full membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers, or,

Appropriate degree or equivalent qualification and general registration with the Psychology Board of Australia,

Appropriate Degree or equivalent qualification which entitles registration as an Occupational Therapist with the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia or,

Appropriate Degree or equivalent qualification which entitles registration as a Physiotherapist with the Physiotherapy Board of Australia.
